title: Assesment of the visual stimuli properties in P300 paradigm
description: EEG recordings from 19 participants performing a P300 speller-style visual stimulation paradigm, designed to assess how stimulus properties affect brain responses and classification accuracy. Each participant completed three sessions with varying numbers of stimuli (4 to 9) and two flash types, a standard flash and a flash superimposed with a cartoon face. Eight scalp channels (Fz, Cz, P3, Pz, P4, PO7, PO8, Oz) were sampled at 256 Hz, together with timestamps and event markers encoding the experimental phases.
methods_description: Eight EEG channels placed per the 10-20 system (Fz, Cz, P3, Pz, P4, PO7, PO8, Oz), grounded at AFz and referenced to the right mastoid (M2), sampled at 256 Hz. Each block comprised Fixation, Target Presentation, Preparation, Stimulation and Rest phases, with markers encoding phase boundaries and the activated symbol. Each of three sessions contained seven recordings varying in stimulus count (4-9) and flash type (standard flash vs cartoon face).
